module_title: My Clinic — Welcome On Board: My Clinic & HR Essentials
audience: All new employees (clinical and non-clinical), day 1–3
objective: Link My Clinic's purpose, values and 7C strategy to daily work, and apply ethics, patient rights, leave, GOSI, overtime, HR systems (Oracle, Qiwa, Mumaris), ID, dress-code and resignation rules.

screens.purpose: Open: make the learner welcome and say what the next 45 minutes give them
screens.visual_concept: Official navy gradient cover with supplied white My Clinic lock-up at upper left, purple module chip, large white petal watermark cropped off the right edge, white title and mist subtitle; no photograph or generated logo.

imagery.description: background-title-navy.png: official My Clinic navy title-gradient background, 16:9.
logo-horizontal-white.png: supplied white My Clinic lock-up, placed top-left at 48 px tall.
imagery.alt_text: My Clinic logo.

imagery.description: mark-white.png: supplied five-petal watermark at 10% opacity, 520 px, cropped off the right edge.

screens.purpose: Explain: the purpose, mission and goal, in plain words, and why it matters on the job
screens.visual_concept: Three stacked statement blocks on an off-white field, each with a small line icon (heart, globe-and-heart, shield-check); the purpose block is largest and sits alone at the top
screens.layout: L3 Content (`full_media` with the hero photo behind a 60% `light` scrim, text blocks left-aligned over it)

imagery.description: hr-img-hero: Reused from `hr-000`, darker crop, scrim applied in the theme, not baked in

screens.on_screen_text: **Purpose** — helping people live longer, healthier, happier lives · **Mission** — the world's most customer-centric healthcare company · **Goal** — outstanding patient experience + excellent clinical outcomes

screens.purpose: Explore: an unscored icebreaker that makes the learner commit to something they care about before any policy appears
screens.visual_concept: Five large tappable option cards in a single row on small screens, two rows on wide; each card has a line icon above a one-word label; a free-text box slides in under the row labelled “Other”
screens.on_screen_text: If you had one million Saudi riyals, where would you spend it?
screens.interaction: Pick the one closest to you, or write your own.

screens.purpose: Explain: each value is a set of behaviours, not a poster
screens.visual_concept: Four horizontal tab labels use the supplied official square value tiles with white line icons; the active panel shows its theme line in large type and actions as plain HTML text.

imagery.description: value-tile-collaborative-burgundy.png: official square value tile with white line icon; tab label remains HTML text.
value-tile-responsible-magenta.png: official square value tile with white line icon; tab label remains HTML text.
value-tile-ambitious-teal.png: official square value tile with white line icon; tab label remains HTML text.
value-tile-caring-purple.png: official square value tile with white line icon; tab label remains HTML text.

screens.on_screen_text: Values are behaviours. Open each one and look for something you already do.

screens.purpose: Check: recognise the four values in real workplace behaviour
screens.visual_concept: Two columns: six plain white action cards on the left, four value tiles on the right; a drawn connector line follows the learner's pointer while a card is selected
screens.on_screen_text: Six things people did this week. Match each one to the value behind it.
screens.interaction: Match each action to a value.

screens.purpose: Explain: where the company is going, and which pillar the learner's own role touches most
screens.visual_concept: Seven collapsed rows in a single column, each with a line icon, the pillar name in caps and a chevron; expanding a row reveals the headline line and the key points as a wrapped keyword row

imagery.description: hr-img-7c-icons: Line icons redrawn from slide 10: headset (Closer), syringe (Cure), mind-and-gears (Capabilities), handshake (Culture), stethoscope (Clinicians), heart-hands (Care), coins (Cost)

screens.on_screen_text: Seven pillars. Open the ones your role touches — you're not expected to memorise all seven.

screens.purpose: Check: pick the pillar a real activity belongs to, with plausible neighbouring pillars as distractors
screens.visual_concept: Stem in large type at the top; four plain option rows beneath, each a radio control plus a single sentence; no imagery, so the decision is the only thing on screen

screens.purpose: Explain: the three groups we serve, including people who are healthy today
screens.visual_concept: Three equal cards side by side, each with one line icon above a short label and a one-line caption; the first card is annotated “sick or healthy” in a smaller line

imagery.description: hr-img-serve-icons: Line icons: family group, community ring, briefcase-and-shield

screens.on_screen_text: Patients & families — sick or healthy · Community · Corporates & insurers

screens.purpose: Explain: how one clinic in 2017 became a network, and what each step added
screens.visual_concept: A single horizontal axis with nine year nodes; the active node lifts and its caption card slides in beneath the axis; a thin progress line fills as the learner moves along
screens.on_screen_text: From one clinic in Jeddah to a network across the west and Riyadh.

screens.purpose: Explore: connect the branch codes staff use every day to real places
screens.visual_concept: Minimal outline map of western Saudi Arabia with an inset for Riyadh; seven numbered pins; each pin opens a small card with the code, the branch type, the city and the year; a counter shows “3 of 7”

imagery.description: hr-img-map: 1200×800, simplified outline of the western region plus a Riyadh inset; no satellite detail; seven pin positions marked but pin graphics drawn by the player
imagery.alt_text: Map of My Clinic sites: five in Jeddah, one in Petro-Rabigh, one in Riyadh.

screens.on_screen_text: Seven sites. You'll hear these codes every day — open each pin.

screens.purpose: Explain: who leads the company and what each role looks after
screens.visual_concept: Four portrait cards in one row; each is a soft-cornered square with the role printed under it and a one-line “looks after” caption; no names until consent is recorded
screens.layout: L3 Content (`text` (blocks: caption, image, caption, image …))

imagery.description: hr-img-leaders-ceo: Consented portrait, 800×800, neutral studio background
imagery.alt_text: Abdullah Alghamdi, Chief Executive Officer.

imagery.description: hr-img-leaders-cmo: Consented portrait, 800×800
imagery.alt_text: Dr Ahmed Al Zahrani, Chief Medical Officer.

imagery.description: hr-img-leaders-coo: Consented portrait, 800×800
imagery.alt_text: Hesham Abdulwahab, Chief Operating Officer.

imagery.description: hr-img-leaders-cfo: Consented portrait, 800×800
imagery.alt_text: Richard Thompson, Chief Finance Officer.

screens.on_screen_text: Chief Executive Officer · Chief Medical Officer · Chief Operating Officer · Chief Finance Officer

screens.purpose: Explore: the accreditation and awards, and the point that they have to be re-earned
screens.visual_concept: Five cards in a shallow fan across the middle of the stage; flipping one rotates it on its vertical axis to reveal the back; the flipped card stays face-up and slides to the back of the fan

imagery.description: hr-img-award-icons: Two line icons redrawn from slides 17–18: a trophy and a laurel star

screens.on_screen_text: Flip each card. Accreditation is measured, not given — and it has to be earned again.

screens.purpose: Explain: the four ethics values, and the one rule to follow when a situation is unclear
screens.visual_concept: Four value blocks in a 2×2 grid with one line icon each; a single full-width warning strip below the grid carries the 24-hour rule, set in `dark` on an `accent`-tinted panel, with an exclamation icon so the meaning is not carried by colour

imagery.description: hr-img-ethics-icons: Line icons: two people with a heart (Respect), open hand with a tick (Integrity), clipboard with a check (Accountability), lightbulb with a link (Innovation and collaboration)

screens.on_screen_text: Respect · Integrity · Accountability · Innovation & collaboration · **Ethical dilemma? Incident report within 24 hours + ethics team.**

screens.purpose: Practise: disclose a conflict of interest, resist a queue-jumping request, and use the 24-hour route when unsure
screens.visual_concept: A flat-illustration band across the top that changes with the node — a meeting room, then a corridor, then a quiet desk; the situation text sits on a white card below it and the choices are full-width buttons under that

imagery.description: hr-img-ethics-meeting: Flat meeting-room scene: table, four chairs, a laptop and a document; two brand colours
imagery.alt_text: A small meeting room where a supplier evaluation is being discussed.

imagery.description: hr-img-ethics-corridor: Flat corridor scene: reception desk and a queue of two patients
imagery.alt_text: A clinic corridor with a reception desk and two patients waiting.

imagery.description: hr-img-ethics-desk: Flat desk scene: laptop showing a blank report form, a cup, a notebook
imagery.alt_text: A desk with a laptop open on an incident report form.

imagery.description: hr-char-noor` / `mentor-noor: Program mentor, three poses
imagery.alt_text: Noor, a senior nurse and safety liaison, speaking.

screens.on_screen_text: Three moments, three decisions. Nobody is watching.
screens.interaction: Choose what you would do at each step.

screens.purpose: Check: separate what patients can expect from us and their families from what we ask of them
screens.visual_concept: Two tall drop zones side by side with plain headings and one line icon each; nine draggable chips sit in a wrap row below; a placed chip shows a 1 px border and a small position number
screens.on_screen_text: Nine statements from the notice in reception. Sort them into the right column.
screens.interaction: Place each statement under Patient right or Patient responsibility.

screens.purpose: Check: apply the right to refuse treatment in a realistic consultation moment
screens.visual_concept: Stem in large type; four plain option rows; no imagery, so the decision carries the screen

screens.purpose: Explain: the three places help comes from, so the learner stops guessing
screens.visual_concept: Three cards in a row, each with a line icon and a short label; the third card carries a download affordance and a small PDF glyph; beneath them a single line states the rule “if it's a request, it goes through Oracle”

imagery.description: hr-img-help-icons: Line icons: headset (help desk), screen-and-form (Oracle), document-arrow (PDF)

screens.on_screen_text: Your HR help desk — one per business unit · Request everything in Oracle · Full rules: **HR Quick Reference** PDF

screens.purpose: Explain: the nine leave types and the one rule worth remembering per type
screens.visual_concept: Nine collapsed rows, each with a two-letter code chip on the left (AN, SK, WI, MA, EX, SC, HJ, CO, OH), the leave name, and a chevron; expanding shows one sentence of plain text plus a single “watch out” line where a rule trips people up
screens.on_screen_text: Nine types. Open the one you need — the full tables are in the Quick Reference.

screens.purpose: Check: find the annual-leave entitlement for a grade without memorising the table
screens.visual_concept: Two columns: four grade tiles on the left (H, G, F and Consultant, A to E) and four number tiles on the right (30, 27, 25, 22); a connector line follows the selection
screens.on_screen_text: Four grades, four entitlements. Match each grade to its annual leave, in working days.
screens.interaction: Match each grade to its entitlement.

screens.purpose: Explain: walk the sick-leave pay bands end to end, then ask the learner to predict the one variation that matters
screens.visual_concept: A five-row vertical ledger on a white card: each row has a day band on the left, the action in the middle and a “Why?” control on the right; revealing a row slides its rationale panel open beneath the action
screens.interaction: Reveal why each step is taken, one step at a time.

screens.purpose: Practise: eligibility decisions for the four leave types people ask about most
screens.visual_concept: A flat service-desk illustration band at the top that stays constant; below it a single request card with the colleague's first name, role and question, then full-width choice buttons; a “3 of 4 answered” counter sits in the corner

imagery.description: hr-img-leavedesk: Flat office-desk scene: a desk, a laptop, a small plant, two chairs; brand colours, white background
imagery.alt_text: An HR service desk with a laptop and two chairs.

imagery.description: hr-char-noor` / `mentor-noor: Program mentor, poses `explaining` and `neutral`
imagery.alt_text: Noor, a senior nurse and safety liaison, at the leave desk.

screens.on_screen_text: Four colleagues, four questions. You're the one they've asked.

screens.purpose: Practise: a short adaptive set on the leave numbers, so experienced hires finish early and new joiners get more
screens.visual_concept: One question at a time, centred, with three option rows; a thin progress strip at the top fills as items are answered and a small “est. 3 more” hint appears once the estimator has enough data
screens.on_screen_text: Answer until the practice says you're ready. It stops early if you've got it.

screens.purpose: Explain: what the deduction on the payslip is for, and why it is a benefit rather than a loss
screens.visual_concept: A horizontal stacked bar split 9.75 / 11.75 across the full width, labelled “you” and “My Clinic” under each segment and “21.5% total” above; beneath it a single line naming what the contribution buys

imagery.description: hr-img-gosi-bar: 960×200 authored SVG stacked bar, two segments; percentages as real text, not baked in
imagery.alt_text: GOSI contribution: the employee pays 9.75%, My Clinic pays 11.75%, a total of 21.5%.

screens.on_screen_text: General Organization for Social Insurance · Saudi employees only · 9.75% you + 11.75% My Clinic = **21.5%** of basic + housing

screens.purpose: Explain: the GOSI calculation step by step, before the learner does one alone
screens.visual_concept: A three-row calculation ledger: each row shows one line of arithmetic in large mono-ish numerals with a “Why?” control to the right; the final row is boxed and carries the answer in the accent colour plus a SAR label
screens.interaction: Reveal why each step is taken, one step at a time.

screens.purpose: Check: do the GOSI calculation once, unaided
screens.visual_concept: A large centred equation with a single inline input at the blank; beneath it a small muted line reminding the learner of the two inputs, and nothing else — no imagery to distract from the arithmetic
screens.on_screen_text: Basic 6,000 + housing 1,500. Your monthly GOSI deduction = ___ SAR

screens.purpose: Explain: the hourly rate first, then the multiplier, so the learner can rebuild it from memory
screens.visual_concept: A three-row ledger like `hr-051`, but the third row forks into two stacked results — “normal day ×1.5” and “public holiday ×2” — so the learner sees one rate and two multipliers
screens.interaction: Reveal why each step is taken, one step at a time.

screens.purpose: Check: apply the overtime formula to a normal working day
screens.visual_concept: Stem in large type; four plain option rows, each a single amount; no imagery, so the arithmetic carries the screen

screens.purpose: Check: route each HR task to the right system, so the learner stops emailing HR
screens.visual_concept: Two columns: six task cards on the left, four system tiles on the right, each system tile carrying a small monogram (O, Q, M, I); a connector line follows the selection
screens.on_screen_text: Six tasks, four systems. Match each task to where it happens.
screens.interaction: Match each task to its system.

screens.purpose: Practise: complete the five Oracle clicks for an annual-leave request on a test account
screens.visual_concept: A browser-chrome frame holding a full-width screenshot; a numbered instruction bar sits directly above the frame; the correct region is not outlined until the learner asks for a hint, at which point a dashed rectangle appears around it

imagery.description: hr-img-oracle-1: Oracle Applications Cloud sign-in page, test account, 1920×1080
imagery.alt_text: Oracle sign-in page with empty username and password fields and a Sign In button.

imagery.description: hr-img-oracle-2: Oracle home with the Time and Absences tile
imagery.alt_text: Oracle home page with a Time and Absences tile in the quick actions area.

imagery.description: hr-img-oracle-3: Time and Absences hub with the Add Leaves tile
imagery.alt_text: Oracle Time and Absences page with an Add Leaves tile.

imagery.description: hr-img-oracle-4: Add Leaves form with the leave-type drop-down open, showing Annual, Bereavement, Marriage, Scientific, Sick, Study
imagery.alt_text: Oracle Add Leaves form with the leave-type drop-down open.

imagery.description: hr-img-oracle-5: Add Leaves form filled, with a Submit button
imagery.alt_text: Oracle Add Leaves form with dates entered and a Submit button.

screens.on_screen_text: Five steps. These screenshots come from a test account, so nothing here is real.
screens.interaction: Follow the instruction on each step and click the right place.

screens.purpose: Check: the licence-renewal rule that can stop someone working
screens.visual_concept: The statement in large type centred, with two wide side-by-side buttons beneath labelled True and False; no imagery, so the judgement carries the screen

screens.purpose: Explain: how to look after the ID card, and what the benefits package actually contains
screens.visual_concept: A two-card row: the left card shows an ID badge with a small warning line about lost cards; the right card is a six-segment benefits wheel, each segment labelled with a one- or two-word benefit and a line icon
screens.layout: L3 Content (`text` (blocks: image, caption, image, caption))

imagery.description: hr-img-idcard: Flat ID badge on a lanyard, first name only, no real logo until approved
imagery.alt_text: A My Clinic staff ID badge on a lanyard.

imagery.description: hr-img-benefits-wheel: 600×600 six-segment wheel: health insurance, performance bonus, development, hybrid work, internal advancement, discounts; labels as real text
imagery.alt_text: Benefits wheel: health insurance, annual performance bonuses, employee development, hybrid work, internal advancement and discounts.

screens.on_screen_text: Lost card → email HR. Replacement fee ⚠ PENDING B4. Damaged card → replaced free.

screens.purpose: Check: apply the dress code that applies to your own role
screens.visual_concept: Three drop zones in a row, each headed by a small flat figure illustration showing the outfit; six draggable chips sit in a wrap row beneath; a placed chip shows a border and an index number

imagery.description: hr-img-dress-frontoffice: Flat figure in a clinic uniform, standing, neutral background
imagery.alt_text: A front-office colleague in the clinic uniform.

imagery.description: hr-img-dress-medical: Flat figure in scrubs and a coat, with a stethoscope
imagery.alt_text: A clinical colleague in scrubs and a coat.

imagery.description: hr-img-dress-backoffice: Flat figure in business attire
imagery.alt_text: A back-office colleague in business attire.

screens.on_screen_text: Six rules, three groups. Place each rule where it applies.
screens.interaction: Place each rule under Front office, Medical team or Back office.

screens.purpose: Explain: how the contract is accepted, and how to leave well if it ever comes to that
screens.visual_concept: A short horizontal four-step strip — Qiwa, Oracle, two months, 15 days — with an arrow between each; each step carries a one-line caption beneath it and a small line icon above

imagery.description: hr-img-exit-icons: Line icons: document-signature (Qiwa), screen-and-form (Oracle), calendar (notice period), envelope-with-certificate (EOS)

screens.on_screen_text: Accept your contract on Qiwa · Resign in Oracle · Notice: **2 months** both ways · EOS + experience certificate within 15 days

screens.purpose: Check: apply the notice rule when the learner's own interests pull the other way
screens.visual_concept: Stem in large type; four plain option rows; no imagery, so the decision carries the screen

screens.purpose: Close: show results by objective and point the learner at what to revisit
screens.visual_concept: Six rows, each with the objective name, a thin bar showing the percentage, and the points earned over points available; any row below the threshold expands to show one line of advice beneath it
screens.on_screen_text: One row per objective. Anything below 70% comes with a suggestion.

screens.purpose: Close: say what the learner can now do, and hand them the two things they need next
screens.visual_concept: A five-item checklist on the left, each with a small tick glyph; on the right two stacked action cards — one for the HR Quick Reference download, one for the onboarding survey — and a single line naming the next module
screens.on_screen_text: You can now: live the values · raise a concern · answer leave and pay questions · use Oracle, Qiwa and Mumaris · keep your licence valid
